orders.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. G. NARENDAR
AND 
HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE ASHISH NAITHANI
16TH SEPTEMBER, 2025
WRIT PETITION (M/B) NO. 730 OF 2025
Hillways Construction Company Pvt. Ltd. …...Petitioner.
Versus
Superintending Engineer & others ….Respondents.
Counsel for the Petitioner : Mr. Siddhartha Singh and Mr. D.S. 
Negi, learned counsel.
Counsel for the State : Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing 
Counsel with Mr. J.C. Pande, learned 
Standing Counsel.
Counsel for the Respondent No.5 : Mr. D.S. Patni, learned Senior Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, 
learned counsel.
ORDER:(per Mr. G. Narendar, C.J.)
The instant writ petition was preferred by the 
petitioner on 23.08.2025 to seek the following reliefs:-
“(i) Issue orders, directions, writ in the nature of certiorari 
quashing the order dated 21.08.2025 (Annexure No.2) whereby the 
petitioner has been held as ineligible for consideration of Technical 
Bids and order dated 22/ 23.08.2025 (Annexure No.3), issued by 
respondent nos.1, 2, 3 whereby the Financial Bids have been 
opened and respondent no.5 has been declared as Lowest One (L￾1).
(ii) Issue orders, directions, writ in the nature of mandamus 
directing respondent no.1, 2, 3 to undertake the Technical and 
Financial Bid opening exercise de-novo after considering the 
Technical and Financial Bid of the petitioner.”
2. We have heard the learned counsel for the 
petitioner, learned Chief Standing Counsel for the State, 
and learned Senior Counsel appearing for respondent 
no.5.
1 3. Prima facie, Annexure-9 would demonstrate that 
the assuring Bank, i.e. HDFC Bank, has sent a code 
IFN-760 cover message regarding the issuance of Bank 
Guarantee in favour of the petitioner.
4. Annexure-9 reads as under:-

ICICI BANK LTD., KHASRA NO.499, NEA
CE, HARIDWAR ROAD, DHRADUN, UTTARA”
5. A bare reading of Annexure-9 would disclose that 
the same has been acknowledged by the Executive 
Engineer, Public Works Department, P.D., Pithoragarh 
2 on 04.08.2025, and it also details that the message is 
acknowledged at 13 hours 26 minutes and 21 seconds. 
Despite the same, the Tender Scrutiny Committee has 
given a vague reasoning that the Bank Guarantee does 
not comply with Condition 18.2.
6. It is vociferously contended by the learned Chief 
Standing Counsel and the learned Senior Counsel that 
the SWIFT is a global standard for secure international 
bank messaging, while SFMS is developed by the Banks 
for domestic financial messaging and as the message 
has not been sent by the Bank on the SFMS platform, it 
is a violation of the conditions.
7. In short, accepted global standards are of no 
consequences is the argument. Whether such argument 
can be appreciated or not, is something which requires 
hearing.
8. In that view of the matter and also in view of the 
second reason assigned by the Committee for rejecting 
the bid which, prima facie, appears to be contrary to 
the Registration Act and the Stamp Act, and also in 
view of the undisputed fact that the petitioner is the 
3 lowest bidder (L1), we deem it necessary to stay all 
further proceedings.
9. At this stage, learned Senior Counsel would place 
reliance on Paragraph No.27 of the ruling of the High 
Court of Delhi, in the case of “VRC Construction 
(India) Private Limited vs. National Highway 
Authority of India, reported in 2024 SCC OnLine 
Del 8447.” Paragraph No.27 reads as under:-
“27. From the record, this Court finds that the respondent/ 
NHAI had revised the bid security on 20th February, 2024 and 
extended the time for bid security submission till 27th February, 
2024. Though the petitioner appears to have taken immediate steps 
to furnish the ABG of Rs. 4 lakhs on 22nd February, 2024 itself, yet 
due to some error and inadvertence, violated the procedure while 
undertaking the SFMS mode to upload the ABG on the portal. 
Though the mistake appears to be inadvertent, yet the respondent/ 
NHAL cannot be faulted with for having annulled the entire Tender 
on the basis that the action of acceptance of ABG subsequent to the 
date of closure of the bid may be misused as a precedent by 
unscrupulous bides. Weighing the conflicting interests, this Court is 
of the opinion that the action of the respondent/ NHAI inviting the 
petitioner as well as other bidders for a fresh bid has allayed the 
apprehension of misuse so far as the respondent/ NHAL is 
concerned and simultaneously, provided a level playing field to the 
petitioner by giving it another chance to submit its bid afresh.”
10. The facts narrated above would clearly 
demonstrate that this is not a case of omission to 
present the BG and the possession of the Bank 
Guarantee with the Authorities is also not disputed, but 
that it is not properly communicated to the Authorities. 
It is also not the case that the communication by the 
Bank has been rejected by the tender accepting 
authority. It is mere perception that it is not in 
4 accordance with Condition 18.2.
11. As recorded above, in other words, the 
respondents would want this Court to accept that 
adopting international standards is not an acceptable 
standard.
12. Counter-affidavit, if any, by the next date of 
listing.
13. List on 22.09.2025 for final hearing.
14. In the meanwhile, HDFC Bank Ltd- WBO, Santosh 
Tower, 1st Floor, Saharanpur Road Majra, Dehradun￾248001, shall produce the records relating to issuance 
of Bank Guarantee, and also the copies of the message 
conveying the issuance of Bank Guarantee, and the 
acknowledgment of the message at 13 hours 26 
minutes and 21 seconds.
15. This Court had already in one matter directed that 
work orders should neither be issued, nor work be 
commenced during the rains. It is admitted fact that 
the State of Uttarakhand has been receiving copious 
rain. It is relevant to recall that the Chief Secretary had 
5 responded to the said orders of this Court by placing 
material in the form of work flow chart, wherein it was 
stated that during the monsoon, the concerned 
authorities have only been directed to prepare the 
documentation.
16. A copy of this order be forwarded to HDFC Bank 
Ltd- WBO, Santosh Tower, 1st Floor, Saharanpur Road 
Majra, Dehradun- 248001.
________________
G. NARENDAR, C.J.
___________________
ASHISH NAITHANI, J.
Dated: 16th September, 2025
NISHANT

orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON’BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. G. NARENDAR
AND
THE HON’BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
Writ Petition (M/B) No.730 of 2025
25th September, 2025
Hillways Construction Company Private Ltd. ---Petitioner 
Versus
Superintending Engineer & Ors. ---Respondents 
--------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. D.S. Negi, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Siddhartha Singh, 
learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing Counsel for the State of 
Uttarakhand
Mr. D.S. Patni, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Tribhuwan 
Phartiyal, learned counsel for respondent no.5.
--------------------------------------------------------------
Per: Sri G. NARENDAR, C. J.
1. Registrar (Judicial) has sought for extension of 
time to place on record the statistics regarding the 
number of petitions filed by petitioner challenging the 
decision of the Tender Evaluation Committee and award 
of tender to persons who are not L1. Request is 
accepted. Further four weeks’ time is granted to the 
Registrar (Judicial).
2. The documents placed today by the HDFC Bank 
clearly records that the Send Receive Date was 
1 04.08.2025 at 13:57 Hrs and the status recorded is 
received. The receipt has been further confirmed by the 
recipient bank i.e. ICICI by email dated 22.09.2025 in 
response to email sent by the petitioner’s banker namely 
HDFC Bank. Despite this, an audacious statement is 
made by the respondent, that the message regarding the 
purchase of bank guarantee has not been sent by the 
issuing Bank, in our opinion, would only reflect to the 
levels that the respondents are stooping to favour a 
particular tenderer. Prima facie, this is the only opinion 
that we are able to infer. 
3. That apart, the HDFC Bank has also placed a 
communication of the RBI dated 25.02.2016 wherein the 
RBI has intimated to all the banks regarding the approval 
of the use of SWIFT also for domestic financial 
transactions. The communication reads as under:-
“RBI approves SWIFT India Domestic Services 
Private Limited (SIDSPL) for Domestic Financial 
Messaging Services in India
The Reserve Bank of India has granted approval to 
SWIFT India Domestic Services Private Limited (SIDSPL) 
to provide messaging services for domestic financial 
transactions in India.
Background
2 The decision to permit the use of SWIFT for domestic 
financial transactions was announced in the Monetary 
Policy Statement 2012-13. Currently, the messaging for 
inter-bank transactions in India is through Structured 
Financial Messaging System (SFMS). Messaging 
operations of SWIFT will support and strengthen the 
infrastructure for financial transactions in the country. 
Alpana Killawala
Principal Advisor” 
4. A reading of the above press release of the RBI 
would obviate any discussion on the aspect. It records 
messaging operations of SWIFT will support and 
strengthen the infrastructure for financial transactions in 
the country. The statement speaks for itself. 
5. That apart, the reply forwarded by the ICICI 
Bank i.e. the bankers of the respondent tendering 
authority to the HDFC Bank clearly shows that the 
intimation regarding purchase of bank guarantee by the 
petitioner favouring the official respondent has been 
communicated by the issuing/assuring bank i.e. the 
HDFC bank on 04.08.2025 and the same communication 
has been received at 13:57 Hrs and the status recorded 
is “received” which is further confirmed by the email 
dated 22.09.2025.
3 6. Per contra, the learned C.S.C. would attempt to 
place reliance on the instructions dated 08.03.2016
issued by the Ministry of Finance, which reads as under:-
“F. No. 7/112/2011-BOA
Government of India Ministry of Finance
Department of Financial Services
Jeevan Deep Building
Parliament Street,
New Delhi the 8th March, 2016
To
1. All Ministries / Departments of Central Government,
2. All Chief Secretaries of States / Union Territories
Subject: Instructions to all Ministries/Departments regarding 
use of SFMS for sending and receiving Letter of 
Credit and Bank Guarantee instruments.
====
Madam / Sir,
I am directed to refer to the subject cited above and request 
your Ministry /Department to give Name of the Beneficiary and his 
details, Beneficiary Branch Indian Financial System Code (IFSC). 
Beneficiary Bank Branch Name and address while giving their 
requirements for the Bank Guarantee, so that the issuing Bank 
Branch can send the IFN 760 COV Bank Guarantee Advice Message 
to the Advising Bank Branch (Beneficiary Bank branch) through 
Structured Financial Messaging System (SFMS), only after which 
the paper Bank Guarantee could become operative.
Yours faithfully,
(Tidk/Ram)
Under Secretary to the Government of India
Tel. No. 23748750
Email: boa@nic.in/usboa-dfs@nic.in
Copy for information to:
1. The Chief General Manager, Department of Banking 
Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai.
2. The Chief Executive, Indian Banks' Association, Central 
4 Office, Mumbai.”
7. It is no more res integra that in matters of 
banking practices the Reserve Bank of India rules the 
roost. In that view, matter requires consideration. 
8. Impleadment Application (IA No.4/2025) is 
allowed. Petitioner to amend the cause title and file 
amended memo of parties by tomorrow. Name of 
Standing Counsel appearing for HDFC Bank – sixth 
respondent Ms. Menka Tripathi may be printed in the 
cause list. 
9. List on 08.10.2025 for disposal in 
supplementary cause list. Interim order granted earlier
is extended till further orders.
 (G. NARENDAR, C. J.)
 
 (SUBHASH UPADHYAY, J.)
Dated: 25.09.2025
R/SS

Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel along with Mr. 
D.S. Negi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. S.N. Babulkar, learned Advocate General, Mr. 
C.S. Rawat, learned C.S.C. along with Mr. J.C. Pandey, 
learned Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. D.S. Patni, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. 
Karmanya Pandey, learned counsel for respondent no.5.
4. Ms. Menka Tripathi, learned counsel for respondent 
no.6.
5. Learned Advocate General submits that the work 
order for the construction of the road in Pithoragarh was 
issued in favour of respondent no.5 which was put to 
challenge in the present writ petition and the Hon’ble Court 
vide interim order dated 16.09.2025 stayed all further 
proceedings.
6. He submits that the road being located in the border 
area is of strategic importance and that due to the interim 
order granted by the Court the work of public importance is 
affected.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner submits 
that the interim order was passed in presence of the parties 
after hearing them at length, however, he fairly admits that 
the construction of road is of strategic importance.
8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, we are 
inclined to modify the order dated 16.09.2025, subject to 
the condition that the successful bidder shall prepare a fix 
deposit of ₹2 Crore in the name of Registrar General, 
Uttarakhand High Court for a period of six months and shall 
furnish the same before the Court within two weeks from  today so that, in case, the writ petition is allowed then the 
Court may consider to award appropriate damages to the 
petitioner.
9. In case the aforesaid FDR is deposited within two 
weeks from today the successful bidder would be permitted 
to carry on the construction work of the road. In default of 
compliance of this order, the interim order dated 
16.09.2025 shall revive against the respondents.
10. List this case after vacation.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.) 
 06.01.2026 06.01.2026
